items.text: the team hub · a Qdrant server
same conflict id on both · worked out apart
key: Sharma wedding edit · due date

captions.text: Tanishk takes the client's call on set.
Lakshya gets the client's email in the office.
Same job. Two dates. Nobody notices…
…until the client does.
When two people disagree, it asks instead of guessing.
Two laptops. Each keeps its own memory.
The hub only relays what the team shares.
Ask anything. Answered on the laptop in 9 ms.
Every line cites its source.
Tanishk loses the hub. No signal on set.
Still remembers. Still answers. 11 ms.
He notes the client's call. Offline.
Turned into a claim, with its source. Queued, not sent.
Meanwhile, the client emails Lakshya: the 16th.
Her laptop reads it and syncs it to the team.
Tanishk can't see it yet.
Both laptops catch the same conflict. On their own.
Qdrant says same job: 0.85, over the 0.82 bar.
Nothing is overwritten. Nothing wins by default.
Ask again: it won't guess. Disputed, with both sources.
Who said what, and where.
Lakshya can ask. Only the owner decides.
Tanishk keeps the 18th. Everyone has it a second later.
Private notes never leave the laptop.
Device-only claims on the hub: 0. Counted live.
Under the hood: every laptop is a full edge node.
Qdrant Edge on the laptop. A Qdrant server as the hub.
Sync is an outbox. Laptops pull what changed.
The trick: a vector of what a claim is about.
Same task, worded differently: 0.85. The bar is 0.82.
Same thing, different value: a conflict.
Where it's going: a private assistant on every laptop.
It knows you, because nothing leaves your laptop.
The direction, not the demo: phone, voice and nudges come next.
Only team work is shared. Everything else stays yours.
Shared memory for small teams that work where the signal doesn't.
